text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Monday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- A cargo train on the Riga-Ventspils line smashed into a lorry on Sunday 91 kilometers west of Riga, disrupting activity at the port. All railway cargo bound for Ventspils was suspended for 24 hours.
- A new Labour party was formed on Saturday. Aivars Kreituss was elected chairman of the party.

- On Saturday the Council of the party Fatherland & Freedom appealed to its representatives in local governments to enter into a coalition with the national ruling parties. Today the party is due to form a joint faction with the national conservative party, the LNNK.The Fatherland & Freedom party has officially nominated Andris Argalis as its candidate to the post of mayor of Riga.

- A Latvian parliamentary delegation including speaker Alfreds Chepanis and deputies Imants Daudishs, Viktors Kalnberzs and Olgerts Dunkers has left for a visit to China. The visit will focus on three joint-economic projects: a $6 million investment in a chip-board production plant in Latvia; the Chinese shipping line between Riga and Hamburg; and the opening of a Chinese trade center in Riga and the setting up of joint ventures.
- The Russian Weather service reports an ozone hole above the Baltics.

- The Latvian Privatisation Agency approved on Friday the basic principles for the privatisation of the hotel Latvia. Norway's Varner Hakon Invest has expressed interest in participating in the hotel's privatization.
- According to preliminary estimates, the national air company Air Baltic has finished the year 1996 with a loss of almost $15 million.
